investment_signals.headline: Spotify reached 300 million Premium subscribers and 777 million MAUs in Q2 2026.
investment_signals.detail: Premium subscribers were 300 million, up 9% year over year, while monthly active users were 777 million, up 12%. Total revenue was €4,777 million, gross margin was 33.4%, and operating income was €655 million.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify Premium ARPU rose 7% year over year to €4.89 in Q2 2026.
investment_signals.detail: Premium revenue grew 15% year over year to €4,331 million. Premium ARPU was €4.89, up 7% year over year, with management attributing growth to price-increase benefits partly offset by product and market mix.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify reported record Q2 2026 profitability and cash generation.
investment_signals.detail: Gross margin was 33.4%, up 193 basis points year over year, and operating income was €655 million. Free cash flow was €797 million in Q2 and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was €3.3 billion.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify guided to 305 million Premium subscribers and €5.0 billion of revenue for Q3 2026.
investment_signals.detail: Q3 guidance was 788 million MAUs, 305 million Premium subscribers, approximately €5.0 billion total revenue, 32.9% gross margin and €670 million operating income. Management also said it expected meaningful year-over-year free-cash-flow growth in 2026.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify said selected markets would receive Premium price updates from September 2025; the announcement did not enumerate countries or tiers.
investment_signals.detail: Spotify said subscribers across South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific would receive emails over the following month explaining the update. It directed new subscribers to local pricing and did not publish a country-by-country price table.
investment_signals.metric_value: Regions listed; country/tier amounts not stated

investment_signals.headline: Spotify announced a $1 US Premium Individual price increase to $12.99.
investment_signals.detail: Reuters reported that Spotify would raise the US monthly Premium price from $11.99 to $12.99. The new price was to take effect on consumers’ billing dates starting in February 2026; Estonia and Latvia were also named.

investment_signals.headline: Spotify raised UK Individual, Duo and Family prices in October 2025.
investment_signals.detail: Music Business Worldwide reported Individual rising from £11.99 to £12.99, Duo from £16.99 to £17.99 and Family from £19.99 to £21.99. Student remained £5.99.

investment_signals.headline: Canada repealed its 3% Digital Services Tax, which Spotify said provided a small one-time Q2 gross-margin benefit.
investment_signals.detail: The Government of Canada said the Digital Services Tax Act repeal received Royal Assent on March 26, 2026 and the tax and related obligations no longer apply. Spotify management said Q2 gross margin benefited modestly from cancellation of the tax through reversal of a prior accrual.

investment_signals.headline: The Mechanical Licensing Collective sued Spotify over audiobook-bundle royalty reporting.
investment_signals.detail: The MLC said Spotify treated Individual, Duo and Family plans with audiobooks as bundled subscription offerings beginning March 2024, affecting the royalty calculation. Spotify’s Q2 2026 filing said the litigation remained pending and included an amended complaint.
investment_signals.metric_value: Pending; plans named: Individual, Duo, Family

key_findings: Spotify’s latest official Q2 2026 results show 300M Premium subscribers (+9% Y/Y), 777M MAUs (+12%), €4,331M Premium revenue (+15%), €4.89 Premium ARPU (+7%), 33.4% gross margin, €655M operating income and €797M free cash flow (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

The current official US Spotify Individual price is $12.99/month, following the January 2026 announcement of a move from $11.99 effective on February billing dates (https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/; https://www.reuters.com/business/spotify-raise-premium-subscription-price-1299-month-select-markets-2026-01-15/).

Spotify’s current Individual price is above Apple Music in the US ($12.99 vs $11.99) but below YouTube Premium ($15.99); this is a sourced local-price observation, not an FX comparison (https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/; https://www.apple.com/apple-music/; https://www.youtube.com/premium).

The UK moved to £12.99 Individual, £17.99 Duo and £21.99 Family in October 2025, with Student held at £5.99 (https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/spotify-raises-uk-and-switzerland-premium-prices-again-as-analysts-see-us-hike-by-early-2026/).

Spotify reported Premium ARPU growth was driven by price-increase benefits partly offset by product/market mix, directly linking headline pricing to the Subscribers × ARPU revenue chain (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Spotify’s Q2 2026 gross margin reached an all-time record 33.4% and Premium gross margin was 34.9%; the deck attributes Premium improvement to revenue growth outpacing music, audiobook and video-podcast costs (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

The August 2025 official pricing announcement was regional rather than country-specific, covering South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific; it did not provide a country/tier schedule (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-08-04/upcoming-changes-to-spotify-premium-subscriptions/).

Current localized coverage is incomplete: Spotify rows were captured for 17 requested countries, while Apple rows cover 10 and YouTube rows only the US; no derived FX comparisons are therefore reported.

No new Spotify price-change announcement dated 2026-09-26 through 2026-09-29 was found in the retrieved Spotify newsroom/IR pages; the latest sourced US change remains the January 15, 2026 announcement (https://newsroom.spotify.com/; https://investors.spotify.com/home/default.aspx; https://www.reuters.com/business/spotify-raise-premium-subscription-price-1299-month-select-markets-2026-01-15/).
analyst_summary.hike_pattern: The sourced history shows a UK multi-tier move announced in October 2025 (Individual +8.3%, Duo +5.9%, Family +10.0%) and a US Individual move announced January 15, 2026 (+8.3%, effective on February billing dates). The August 2025 official announcement indicates a broad regional wave, but does not identify which countries moved first or provide country/tier effective dates; cadence and regional sequencing therefore remain unproven (https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/spotify-raises-uk-and-switzerland-premium-prices-again-as-analysts-see-us-hike-by-early-2026/; https://www.reuters.com/business/spotify-raise-premium-subscription-price-1299-month-select-markets-2026-01-15/; https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-08-04/upcoming-changes-to-spotify-premium-subscriptions/).
bull_points: Premium subscribers grew 9% Y/Y to 300M while Premium revenue grew 15% Y/Y to €4,331M, and ARPU grew 7% to €4.89 (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Gross margin of 33.4%, operating income of €655M and Q2 free cash flow of €797M show pricing and operating leverage reaching reported profitability (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Management’s Q3 guidance calls for 305M Premium subscribers and 32.9% gross margin, while expecting meaningful full-year 2026 free-cash-flow growth (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-26-Earnings-Call-Prepared-Remarks.pdf).
bear_points: The same Q2 deck says Premium ARPU gains were partly offset by product/market mix, so list-price increases do not translate one-for-one into realized ARPU (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

Spotify’s Q2 materials describe ongoing investment in marketing, cloud and AI spend, which can pressure EBIT even as gross margin improves (https://s29.q4cdn.com/175625835/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Shareholder-Deck-FINAL.pdf).

The MLC litigation concerns the royalty treatment of audiobook-inclusive Individual, Duo and Family plans, creating a potential gross-margin/royalty risk (https://www.themlc.com/news/the-mechanical-licensing-collective-brings-legal-action-for-unpaid-royalties-against-spotify-usa-inc).
Current country coverage and competitor reaction evidence are incomplete, preventing a fully comparable global price-premium or churn conclusion.

run_schedule.weekly_production_schedule: Run once per day at 13:15 UTC; compare against the 2026-09-25 baseline and append only newly observed price, promo, reaction, regulatory or earnings facts.

implementation_notes: Use official localized URLs and do not substitute a generic US-dollar page for a country; preserve the exact recurring price separately from introductory or trial copy.
Store one row per country/service/tier and mark tax-inclusive as not stated unless the page explicitly says included/excluded.
For daily runs, hash normalized page price blocks and flag NEW only when price, tier, trial, tax wording, or availability differs from the baseline or prior daily run.
Keep announced_date and effective_date separate; if a source publishes only one, leave the other unknown rather than infer it.
Use an official dated FX source only when all three local individual prices exist; otherwise omit the derived row and append the missing input to data_gaps.
For app stores, record the aggregate rating and count exactly as printed and never calculate sentiment share unless a source supplies a denominator.
